summary.text: Factorization of polynomials expresses a polynomial with coefficients in a given field or in the integers as the product of irreducible factors with coefficients in the same domain.
It is one of the fundamental components of computer algebra systems, and modern algorithms can quickly factor univariate polynomials of degree more than 1000.
Factorization depends on the base field: over the reals the irreducible factors have degree at most two, and over the complex field a polynomial splits into linear factors.

facts.label: Uniqueness
facts.value: Unique up to multiplying factors by invertible constants

facts.label: Over the reals
facts.value: Irreducible factors have degree at most two

facts.label: Over the rationals
facts.value: Irreducible polynomials of any degree exist

facts.label: Gauss's lemma
facts.value: The product of two primitive polynomials is also primitive

facts.label: First algorithm step
facts.value: Square-free factorization comes first in most algorithms

items.prompt: A polynomial has integer coefficients. Over which number system can it be broken all the way down into linear factors?

options.label: The complex numbers
The real numbers
The rational numbers
None, linear pieces are impossible

items.explain: By the fundamental theorem of algebra, a polynomial with integer coefficients can be factored into linear factors over the complex field.

items.prompt: Someone claims that over the reals, a polynomial can have an irreducible factor of degree 5. What is wrong with this?

options.label: Real polynomials cannot be factored at all
Real irreducible factors have degree at most two
Only degree 3 is allowed there
Real factors must all be linear

items.explain: Over the field of reals, the irreducible factors have degree at most two.

items.prompt: A polynomial has two identical factors. What else is true?

options.label: It is a multiple of that factor squared
Its derivative must be exactly zero
It must be irreducible itself
It cannot have any roots at all

items.explain: If two or more factors are identical, the polynomial is a multiple of the factor's square, and the factor also divides the derivative.

items.prompt: You are designing a procedure to factor a large polynomial over the rationals. What should the first step be?

options.label: Multiply it by its own derivative
Find every root by hand
Factor each coefficient first
Split it into square-free factors

items.explain: Square-free factorization is the first step in most polynomial factorization algorithms.

items.prompt: You divide every coefficient of an integer polynomial by their greatest common divisor and set that divisor aside. What do you now hold?

options.label: A square-free factor of it
The derivative of the polynomial
The primitive part of the polynomial
An irreducible factor of degree two

items.explain: The primitive part is the polynomial divided by its content, which is a primitive polynomial with integer coefficients.

items.prompt: A primitive polynomial is known to be irreducible over the rationals. What follows about it over the integers?

options.label: It must split over the integers
It is irreducible over the integers too
It cannot be primitive
Nothing, the two cases are unrelated

items.explain: A primitive polynomial is irreducible over the rationals if and only if it is irreducible over the integers.
